manage.upload_result_summary: {imported} newly imported, {updated} updated (existing activity, new info picked up), {duplicates} unchanged, {skipped} skipped ({unsupported} had an unsupported file type).
manage.nothing_imported: Nothing was imported. Check the container logs (docker compose logs matched-runs) — every skipped file is logged there with the reason (unsupported extension, no GPS data, parse error, etc).
manage.db_export_import_note: Useful for running the initial bulk import and route matching on a faster machine (e.g. a desktop instead of a Raspberry Pi), then moving the already-populated database over to wherever you actually run the app day to day.
manage.ingress_import_warning: You're viewing this through Home Assistant's ingress sidebar right now. If your database is larger than ~16MB, importing it here will fail with "Maximum request body size exceeded" - that's a hardcoded Supervisor limit on ingress traffic, not something this app can work around. Use port 8000 instead for the import specifically - http://<your-ha-host>:8000/manage - not port 8123 (Home Assistant's own port still goes through the same ingress limit even on your local network - it's specifically the port number that matters here, not whether the address is local or public). Export/download isn't affected, only import.
manage.import_replaces_note: Importing completely replaces all current data - there's no merge. Make sure that's really what you want before confirming.
manage.upload_size_limit_note: A large bulk import (a full export folder, especially with many activities) can hit an upload size limit imposed by whatever's in front of this app, not by the app itself - Home Assistant's ingress caps requests at about 16MB, and a Cloudflare Tunnel or similar reverse proxy commonly caps them around 100MB on free/pro plans. If a large import fails partway through with a "413" or "Payload Too Large" error (possibly showing a Cloudflare or Home Assistant error page rather than anything from this app), that's what's happening. Use port 8000 for large imports instead - http://<your-ha-host>:8000/manage - not Home Assistant's own port 8123, which still goes through ingress even on your local network and hits the same 16MB limit; it's specifically the port number that matters, not whether the address is local or public. Port 8000 bypasses both limits at once.
manage.upload_files_note: Select as many files as you like at once — e.g. your whole unzipped Garmin or Strava export folder (Strava: Settings → My Account → Download or Delete Your Account → Request Your Archive), or use "Upload entire folder" to pick the folder directly. GPX, FIT, and TCX are all supported, including gzip-compressed files (.gpx.gz / .fit.gz / .tcx.gz, as Strava's export uses). If your Strava export's top-level activities.csv is included, your real Strava activity titles are recovered automatically (works even if uploaded separately, after the fact, to backfill names on what's already imported). Files without GPS data (indoor activities) are skipped automatically.
manage.strava_not_configured: Strava sync not configured (set STRAVA_CLIENT_ID / SECRET in .env to enable)
manage.merge_types_unchanged: No activities matched {from_types} - nothing was changed.
manage.merge_types_note: Useful if the same real activity ended up logged under different type labels - e.g. an old watch only offering a limited choice of types, so the same kind of outing was "Walking" one year and "Hiking" another. Pick any number of existing types above, and a destination type to relabel them all to (an existing one, or type a new name). Optionally restrict this to activities before a given date, leaving anything after as-is.
manage.rename_confirm: This renames EVERY activity to '[City] [Activity Type]' (e.g. 'Zurich Running'), overwriting current names. Continue?
manage.rename_by_city_note: Renames every activity to "[City] [Activity Type]" using its start location (e.g. "Zurich Running"), looked up via OpenStreetMap's free geocoding service. That service limits lookups to about one per second, so this can take a while for a large history - progress is shown below once started. Activities at the same location only need one lookup, so it's much faster after the first run. Indoor activities with no GPS track are left untouched.
manage.garmin_autosync_on: Automatic sync is on — checking for new activities every {interval} minutes.
manage.garmin_env_fallback_note: A GARMIN_EMAIL/GARMIN_PASSWORD fallback is configured in .env, but no saved login session was found yet.
manage.garmin_unofficial_note: Uses an unofficial method (there's no public Garmin API for personal use), so treat it as best-effort — it can break if Garmin changes their login flow.

strava.scope_denied: Strava did not grant the activity:read_all permission (granted scope: {scope}).
strava.scope_denied_fix: This usually happens when this app was authorized before with a narrower scope, and Strava is silently reusing that old grant. Fix: go to strava.com/settings/apps, revoke access for this app, then connect again.
strava.auth_cleared: Your stored Strava connection was cleared. Please connect Strava again — if this keeps happening, also revoke the app at strava.com/settings/apps first, then reconnect.
